qa.q: What happens to my current website?
qa.a: Three options: we keep it and integrate the booking engine, we redesign it if it needs a refresh, or we start from scratch. We decide at the kickoff.
We migrate customers, historical bookings and configuration from Excel, Google Calendar or other software. No data loss.

qa.q: What if something breaks in the middle of the season?
qa.a: Direct support with the team, not a generic ticket. In high season we're available outside business hours. It's part of the partner model.

onboarding.ctaText: Want to see what your specific implementation would look like? We'll set up a demo with your real fleet.

testimonials.quote: We went from 8 to 22 bookings/day without hiring anyone. The AI closes 70% of WhatsApp inquiries before we even open.
For the first time in five years I see the operation across all three bases on a single screen. And I see it from my phone.
I cut three tools, two spreadsheets and one back-office person. Solnow pays its % with that alone.

items.a: We charge a % on the bookings we generate through our platform + a cost per AI conversation. No fixed fee and no setup fee. Aligned model: if you don't bill, we don't charge.

items.q: How does the commission model work?
items.a: We apply a commission on the GMV of bookings processed by Solnow (engine + WhatsApp AI + OTAs). The exact detail is agreed based on your volume and channel mix at the kickoff.

items.q: Does it work if I don't have stable internet at the base?
items.a: Yes. The boarding app is offline-first: it records QR scans, signatures and check-in without connection and syncs when the signal returns. Critical for docks and areas with intermittent coverage.

items.q: What happens to my data if I leave Solnow?
items.a: Your data is yours. We give you a full export (customers, bookings, contracts, invoices) in CSV + JSON, with no friction and no retention periods.

items.q: Do you handle contracts for minors?
items.a: Yes. Specific templates with fields for legal guardian, parent signature and document validation. Compliant with Spanish regulation and compatible with harbor-master rules.

items.q: Does it integrate with Viator / GetYourGuide?
items.a: Yes, with inventory synced in real time and no overbookings across channels. But for our ICP, OTAs are the lowest-volume channel: the priority is consolidating the front desk, WhatsApp and the web into a single flow. OTAs are a complement, not the center.

items.q: Can I set different prices per season?
items.a: Yes. Prices by season, weekday, time of day, duration and jet ski model. Combinable rules, editable without touching code.

items.q: How is it billed: per booking or monthly?
items.a: Monthly invoice with a breakdown per booking, commission and AI conversations. Automatic settlement via Stripe Connect to your account the following month.

contrato.disclaimer: This template and guide are for guidance only and do not constitute legal advice. Before using the contract with customers, review it with a legal advisor and verify the requirements of your Harbour Master (Capitanía Marítima) and region.

sections.h: What is the rental contract for?

blocks.text: The jet ski rental contract is the written proof of the conditions the customer accepted: which craft they took, in what condition, for how long, what happens if they damage it and who is liable in an accident. Without it, any incident becomes your word against theirs.
It's not red tape: it's what keeps you from paying for a breakdown, a fine or a claim yourself. In practice, a signed contract prevents 90% of the arguments at the desk when the craft comes back.

items: Puts the deposit and the cases where it's withheld in writing
Transfers liability for damage and penalties to the renter
Documents the craft's condition at handover and return
Meets the obligation to inform about the use of personal data

sections.h: What a jet ski rental contract must include

blocks.text: These are the blocks that can't be missing. The downloadable template already has them all; here's why each one matters.

items: Party details: rental company (legal name, tax ID, address) and renter (name, ID or passport, phone).
Craft identification: make, model, registration or hull number and power.
Rental period: date, handover time and agreed return time.
Price, payment method and deposit: amount, method and refund conditions.
Craft condition: description of prior damage and fuel level at handover.
Insurance and coverage: what the policy covers and what excess or damage the customer assumes.
Conditions of use: permitted navigation area, minimum distance from shore and prohibitions (alcohol, number of occupants, etc.).
Liability: the renter is responsible for damage, administrative penalties and third parties during the rental.
Data protection: legal basis and purpose of processing, with reference to the GDPR.
Signature of both parties and date.

sections.h: The most forgotten clauses (and the ones that cost you)

blocks.text: Most free templates online cover the basics but leave out what really protects you when something goes wrong.
Without a liability clause for penalties, Harbour Master fines for navigating out of zone or without a life jacket can end up in your name, because the craft is registered to your company.

items: Excess and cap on damage assumed by the customer, with a specific amount.
Late-return penalty, per hour or fraction.
Customer's statement that they can swim and have received the safety briefing.
Explicit authorization to charge later damage or fines to the card.
Photographic inventory of the craft before and after, attached to the contract.

sections.h: Renting to minors: the contract needs extra fields

blocks.text: If you rent to or carry minors as passengers, you need written consent from the parent or legal guardian. It's not enough for the paying adult to say so verbally.

items: Legal guardian's details and relationship to the minor.
Guardian's signature authorizing the activity.
Validation of the guardian's ID document.
Statement of responsibility for the minor during the activity.

blocks.text: The template includes a specific annex for minors that you can attach only when needed.

hero.h1: Jet ski rental regulations in Spain
hero.lede: What you need to rent jet skis legally in Spain: licensing, insurance, Harbour Master authorizations, navigation zones and mandatory documentation. In a clear guide for operators starting out or getting compliant.

normativa.disclaimer: This guide is for guidance only and does not constitute legal advice. Nautical regulations depend on national, regional and local rules, and on each area's Harbour Master (Capitanía Marítima). Always confirm the current requirements with your Harbour Master and an advisor before operating.

sections.h: What you need to rent jet skis legally

blocks.text: In Spain, jet ski rental (jet skis are considered recreational craft) is regulated by the Directorate-General of the Merchant Marine and supervised by the Harbour Masters, on top of coastal regulations and each region's rules. As an operator you must meet requirements on four fronts: the rider's license, insurance, activity authorizations and documentation.

items: Craft (jet skis) properly registered and with their inspections up to date.
Mandatory civil-liability insurance for each craft.
Authorization to run the activity and, depending on the area, occupation of public domain.
Valid license or authorization for whoever operates the craft.
Logbook and documentation for each rental.

sections.h: Licensing: does the customer need one?

blocks.text: It depends on the craft's power and the rental format. Broadly there are three paths:

items: Navigation license: allows operating limited-power jet skis after a short theory-and-practice course. The usual route for customers who want to ride on their own.
Higher nautical qualification (PNB, PER…): for more powerful craft a higher qualification is required depending on the craft's category.
Guided or 'baptism' format: the customer rides without a license inside a marked circuit under the direct supervision of a qualified instructor. The most common format for tourist rentals.

blocks.text: The classification of craft by power and the qualification required can change; confirm with your Harbour Master which category applies to each model in your fleet.
Beyond the customer, the rental company must be compliant to offer the service.

items: Registration of the economic activity and the corresponding tax compliance.
Authorization for the rental activity and, if you operate from a beach or maritime-terrestrial public domain, the concession or occupation authorization.
Craft registered in the company's name, with technical inspection in force where applicable.
Safety and rescue means required for the activity.
Instructors with the appropriate qualification for the guided format.

blocks.text: Each jet ski must have mandatory civil-liability insurance covering damage to third parties. For your business it's also wise to have broader coverage.

items: Mandatory civil liability per craft (damage to third parties).
Own-damage coverage for the craft, with its excess.
Coverage for the activity and instructors in the guided format.

blocks.text: Renting a craft without mandatory insurance in force is a serious offense and, after an accident, can leave you exposed to respond with your own assets.

sections.h: Navigation zones and distance from shore

blocks.text: Jet skis can't navigate just anywhere. Their use is restricted to protect bathers and the coastline.

items: Departure and return only through the channels or marked zones set up for it.
No navigating inside bathing areas or closer than the minimum distance from shore set by local rules.
Respect for speed and safety distances to bathers, divers and other vessels.
Daytime navigation and within the limits of the authorization.

blocks.text: Each rental generates paperwork you must be able to show in an inspection: the customer contract, the safety-briefing statement and the activity logbook.
Keeping this up to date in peak season is where most operators slip, and where it's easiest for a detail to be missing in an inspection.
Solnow generates the contract and invoice when the booking is confirmed and keeps the logbook compliant with the rules, with nothing to fill in by hand.

Breaches of navigation and maritime-safety rules can mean significant fines and, in serious cases, immobilization of the craft or loss of the authorization. Navigating out of zone, without insurance or without the proper license are among the most penalized.
Because the craft are registered to your company, many penalties arrive in your name even when the offender is the customer. That's why the contract must explicitly transfer that liability.

faq.q: Does the customer need a license to rent a jet ski?
faq.a: It depends on the craft's power and the format. To ride solo you usually need at least a navigation license; for powerful craft, a higher qualification. In the guided or 'baptism' format, the customer can ride without a license inside a marked, supervised circuit.

faq.q: What insurance is mandatory to rent jet skis?
faq.a: Each craft must have mandatory civil-liability insurance covering damage to third parties. For the business, adding own-damage and activity coverage is recommended.

faq.q: Where can jet skis navigate?
faq.a: They can only enter and exit through the authorized channels or marked zones, can't navigate inside bathing areas and must respect the minimum distance from shore and bathers set by local rules. Confirm the exact limits with your Harbour Master.

faq.q: What if a customer commits an offense with my craft?
faq.a: Because the craft is registered to your company, many penalties can arrive in your name. A contract that explicitly transfers liability for damage and fines to the renter is key to passing them on.

faq.q: Do I have to keep a logbook?
faq.a: Yes, the activity requires documenting rentals. See how in our guide on the jet ski logbook.

hero.h1: Jet ski logbook: what it is and how to keep it
hero.lede: What the logbook is, why it can be requested in an inspection, what data each rental must contain and how to keep it up to date without it eating your season.

libro.disclaimer: This guide is for guidance only and does not constitute legal advice. Logbook requirements may vary by Harbour Master and regional rules. Confirm the format and required data with your Harbour Master.

blocks.text: The logbook is the document where the operator records every use of its jet skis: who rented it, when it left and returned, with which craft and under what conditions. It works as your fleet's activity history and is what shows, in an inspection, that you operate in an orderly and traceable way.
It can be kept on paper (one notebook per base) or digitally. What matters is that it's complete, up to date and available when requested.

The rental activity requires keeping documentation and traceability of each operation, and Harbour Masters can require the activity record in an inspection. Although the exact format can vary by area, keeping an orderly logbook is an expected practice and protects you against claims or incidents.
Check with your Harbour Master whether a specific format or a stamped book is required; in some areas the requirement is stricter than in others.

sections.h: What data each entry must contain

blocks.text: Each line of the logbook should let you reconstruct a complete rental. At a minimum:

items: Date and time of departure and return.
Craft identification (registration or hull number).
Details of the customer who rented it (name and ID).
License or format (own license, guided or baptism).
Responsible instructor, if applicable.
Incidents: breakdowns, delays, damage or penalties.
Confirmation that safety equipment was handed over (life jacket, etc.).

sections.h: How to keep the logbook, step by step

items: Before each departure, record the craft, the customer and the departure time.
Record the customer's license or the format (guided or baptism) and the assigned instructor.
Confirm and note the handover of the life jacket and safety gear.
On return, record the return time and any incident (damage, delay, penalty).
Close the entry and file it so you can retrieve it by date, craft or customer.
Periodically check that no data is missing: an incomplete entry is as good as none.

sections.h: Common mistakes that work against you

blocks.text: The most common mistake is filling it in 'later': at the end of the day, from memory. In peak season gaps pile up and, when the inspection or claim arrives, exactly the data for the problem rental is missing.

items: Incomplete or illegible entries.
A single notebook that gets wet, lost or left at another base.
Not recording the format or instructor for baptisms.
No record that safety equipment was handed over.

blocks.text: The logbook is the perfect example of an admin task nobody wants to do and that, nonetheless, protects you. The solution isn't 'write it down better': it's to have it fill itself in.

With Solnow, every rental that goes through the system is recorded automatically: craft, customer, times, format, instructor, contract signature and check-in with QR boarding scan. The logbook is generated compliant with the rules, multi-base and searchable by date, craft or customer, with no one writing anything by hand.
It's part of Solnow's automatic after-sales: logbook, reviews and customer profile, on autopilot when each activity closes.

faq.q: What exactly is the jet ski logbook?
faq.a: It's the document where every use of your fleet's jet skis is recorded (craft, customer, times, conditions and incidents). It serves to prove an orderly, traceable operation in an inspection or a claim.

faq.q: Is keeping a logbook mandatory?
faq.a: The activity requires keeping documentation and traceability of each rental, and Harbour Masters can require it. The exact format can vary by area, so check with your Harbour Master whether a specific format is required.

faq.q: Can I keep it digitally instead of on paper?
faq.a: Yes. A digital record is usually more reliable: it isn't lost, it's legible, it's consulted instantly and it lets you keep one logbook per base without loose notebooks. Check with your Harbour Master whether the digital format is accepted in your area.

faq.q: What data can't be missing from each entry?
faq.a: At a minimum: date and times of departure and return, craft identification, customer details, license or format, instructor if applicable, handover of safety equipment and incidents.

faq.q: How do I automate the logbook?
faq.a: With Solnow each rental is recorded on its own (craft, customer, times, format, instructor, signature and QR check-in) and the logbook is generated compliant, multi-base and searchable. We'll show you in a demo.
